title: Module quiz: Governance, safety and risk

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario: Ines's claims assistant keeps its record of each request for a year, and a reviewer notices that the screen that checks incoming requests is allowed to let them through when it is down. Which change does the first page support?

options.text: Keep the pass-through and add a monitor that alerts on the gap
options.says: Ruled out because the first page puts the monitor in the layers that watch "afterwards", so "an output control cannot stop a tool call that already happened".

options.text: Keep the pass-through and shorten the retention of the records
options.says: Ruled out because retention does not close the gap: "A screen that is down and lets a request through is the opening an attacker waits for".

options.text: Hold each high-consequence call until that service replies
options.says: An input control holds a high-consequence call when it fails.

options.text: Move the screening into the system prompt so that it cannot be down
options.says: Ruled out because "a line in a prompt is a request, and a control is a step the model cannot skip".

origin.section: Four layers, and what each guards

questions.stem: Scenario: A review finds that a model system's average accuracy is 94 percent, and that one language group, a small part of the traffic, scores 70 percent. The team says the system passes. What does the second page say about that claim?

options.text: A small group cannot be measured, so the average stands
options.says: Ruled out because "The groups must be defined where they can be measured", and a language group can be labelled and so reported.

options.text: A headline figure masks the segment that fails
options.says: The page measures fairness as a gap per group and warns that an average hides one.

options.text: The group's score is dropped below the needed volume
options.says: Ruled out because "a headline average hides a failing group exactly as it hides a failing segment", so dropping the score hides it.

options.text: The system passes, as its launch test was broad
options.says: Ruled out because "fairness is a property of outcomes by group", and a broad launch test is not a gap measure.

origin.section: Fairness is a gap you measure

questions.stem: Scenario: An auditor asks a team to prove that a refund over a set amount was approved by a person. The team has an audit entry for the refund with a request id, an outcome of human and a character count. What do they have?

options.text: Nothing, because a record without the content is not admissible
options.says: Ruled out because the design keeps "proof of what happened", and the page does not tie proof to stored content.

options.text: A record that is too thin, since only the text proves what happened
options.says: Ruled out because "Content that was never stored cannot be breached, subpoenaed by accident or kept past a deletion request".

options.text: A record that holds the refund amount and the approver's name
options.says: Ruled out because the entry holds "request id, action, consequence, outcome and the size of the text", which names no amount or approver.

options.text: Evidence of the step, with no copy of the customer's text kept
options.says: The record shows the step happened without a copy of the data.
